title: canary-release-scratchpad
content:
Quick scratchpad for upcoming canary -> GA rollout (serving-runtime v2.14.1). Personal notes + checklist.

Context:
- Target: roll v2.14.1 (includes kernel selection fix + kv-cache GC improvements) to hosted and dedicated pools.
- Motivations: reduce tail 95 latency for long-context workloads; address mem leak under heavy batching.
- Owners: release-engineering (Ethan), SRE (Lina), runtime (Morgan).

Open questions / risks:
- Do we need to pin model variants for fallback? (depends on downstream compat; TODO ask model-onboarding).
- Dedicated customers with strict pinning: confirm contract list and notify PMs.
- Can aria (billing) handle extra request volume from smoke tests? check quota limits.

Rollout plan (high level):
1) Staging -> smoke tests -> internal canary (5%) -> ramp 20% -> 50% -> 100%
2) Timebox each stage (initial): 30m smoke, 2h 5% -> 2h 20% -> 4h 50% -> 24h 100% monitoring before GA opt-in.
3) Automated rollback triggers: see rollback criteria below.

Pinning & version strategy:
- Default runtime image tag: rwinf/serving-runtime:v2.14.1
- For dedicated customers using pinned images, update docs and notify via ticket.
- For hosted: route policy will prefer v2.14.1 for compatible model families; fallback to v2.14.0 if failures detected.
- Note: ensure that the model registry compatibility matrix includes the new kernel ops; PR #1842 touches kernel selector.
- Add a temporary feature flag 'canary-v2-141' in routing config to target traffic.

Namespace / shims checklist (pre-roll):
- [ ] Build and push runtime image (CI pipeline green) -> artifact tag v2.14.1
- [ ] Rollout artifact to staging clusters, run full e2e (integration with kv-cache + long-context tests)
- [ ] Update canary routing policy in control plane (create canary routing policy ID)
- [ ] Create release notes (short) and post in #release-rollouts channel
- [ ] Notify Dedicated customers with pinning contract (email + ticket)
- [ ] Backup snapshot of routing config + consistent diff exported
- [ ] Ensure KMS/HSM access unchanged for private deployments (security team signoff)

Smoke tests (staging):
- Perf: 1k synthetic requests with mixed seq lengths (64/512/2048) -> confirm 95p latency change <= -5% (no regressions on 50p)
- Stability: 100 long-running sessions (chat style) with KV cache warm-up -> no mem growth > 10% over 1h
- Correctness: sample generation checks against golden prompts (eval harness) -> BLEU/ROUGE stable; run basic safety filters
- Observability: ensure traces sampled, token-level cost attributed

Canary rollout steps (detailed):
Stage A: internal (5%)
- [ ] Create canary route: route-id: canary/v2.14.1/internal/2026-03-01
- [ ] Wire canary flag in experiment manager -> target origin header X-Release-Canary: v2.14.1
- [ ] Launch 5% for internal-only customers + ops API keys (low blast radius)
- Monitoring: watch 95p latency, error rate, CPU/GPU utilization, OOMs, inference errors (exception rate), user-facing 5xx
- Duration: 2 hours (if green, proceed).

Stage B: public 20%
- [ ] Expand canary to 20% across hosted low-traffic regions (us-west-2, eu-west-1)
- [ ] Run automated traffic migration jobs (k8s canary controller)
- Monitoring: add business metrics (token cost delta, e2e latency for anchored endpoints), alert thresholds tightened
- Duration: 2–4 hours (stability dependent).

Stage C: 50% -> 100%
- [ ] Gradual doubling every window (50% window 4h, then 100% with 24h observation)
- Note: maintain 10% capacity headroom for autoscaling.

Rollback criteria (auto + manual):
Auto-triggers (immediate rollback):
- Error rate > 0.5% absolute increase over baseline for 5m (http 5xx / model errors)
- 95p latency regression > 30% over baseline for 10m
- OOM/evictions spike or GPU mem leak patterns detected
- Unhandled generation correctness failures > 2% (according to eval harness)
Manual triggers:
- Significant customer reports affecting key accounts (listed in notify list)
- Security or data leak detected (immediate rollback + incident response)

Post-rollback checklist:
- [ ] Pin routing back to previous stable (v2.14.0) and confirm traffic shift
- [ ] Capture diagnostics: profiling dumps, logs, pprof, kernel selector traces
- [ ] Assign incident owner, send initial incident brief to stakeholders
- [ ] Reproduce in staging with traffic pattern captured (replay logs)

Observability / dashboards to watch:
- Canary overview Grafana (linked above)
- Token-level cost per request (Console -> Cost breakdown)
- Per-model / per-route latency heatmap
- KV cache hit/miss ratio + GC events
- Kernel selector histogram (seq-length vs kernel choice)
- Error logs filtered by new runtime op IDs

Quick commands / snippets (ops):
- Promote canary route (example): curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/api/routes/promote -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"route_id":"canary/v2.14.1/internal/2026-03-01","target_percent":20}'
- Rollback: curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/api/routes/rollback -d '{"route_id":"canary/v2.14.1/internal/2026-03-01"}'
- Check build: gh run list -R redwood-inference/serving-runtime --workflow=release.yml

Notes / fragment ideas (to tidy into release notes):
- v2.14.1: kernel selector fix reduces OOMs for long-context batching + GC fixes for kv-cache to avoid mem retention in multi-tenant pools.
- Internal benchmark: 95p latency improved ~12% on 2048 tokens with batching enabled (staging run 2026-02-18).

Things to follow up (post-roll):
- [ ] Update dedicated customer docs + migration guide (Morgan)
- [ ] Add regression tests to CI for kv-cache scenario (Lina)
- [ ] Track cost impact for 2 weeks and report to product/finance
- [ ] Confirm no impact to private deployments (run on-prem smoke with offline PKI)

Misc notes / TODOs: 
- Chase model-onboarding about fallback compatibility matrix (owner: Samir)
- Double-check that the canary flag respects per-tenant overrides (i.e., VIP customers excluded automatically)
- Confirm release window with marketing if release notes are GA-ready

Random brain-dump: always prefer safe rollouts for kernel changes that affect memory; a small 5% internal phase has caught regressions twice this year.

End of scratchpad. Will convert to formal checklist before prod rollout.
